reconcile.note: Gill parses Mark's phrase "in the days of Abiathar" as a loose time marker for the era, not a claim Abiathar already held the priesthood when David ate the bread.

discrepancy.note: Troki charges Mark with an inattentive reading of Samuel, since David went to Ahimelech, not to his son Abiathar.

quotes.text: This author of the Gospel likewise evinces an inattentive perusal of our Scriptures, since David did not go to Abiathar, but he went to Ahimelech, the father of Abiathar.
quotes.attr: Isaac ben Abraham Troki (d. 1594), Faith Strengthened (Chizzuk Emunah), Part II (c. 1593; Eng. transl. 1851), ch. XLV, on Mark 2:26.

sides.snippet: Then came David to Nob to Ahimelech the priest: and Ahimelech came to meet David trembling
sides.verseText: Then came David to Nob to Ahimelech the priest: and Ahimelech came to meet David trembling, and said to him, Why are you alone, and no man with you?

sides.snippet: he entered into the house of God when Abiathar was high priest, and ate the show bread
sides.verseText: How he entered into the house of God when Abiathar was high priest, and ate the show bread, which it is not lawful to eat except for the priests, and gave also to those who were with him?\"
